challengeFindings.title: A second refused flush pushes a `Merge commit '<sha>'` head with no `[skip ci]`, so the reused `ship-failed/{FID}` PR runs the full CI on every later attempt

A reused open PR is merged with `--match-head-commit` straight after the branch push, before GitHub has moved the PR's head to the pushed tip, so GitHub refuses the merge and the record waits for a human
A failed `git add` in `restoreBranchRows` is ignored, so `closePr` commits the merge without the leftover tip's put-back ledger rows and still exits 0 with `pushed: true`

Anyone who can push `ship-failed/{FID}` plants a symlinked `.jsonl` in the run's log folder, and the refused flush's `restoreBranchRows` follows it, creating a file outside the checkout at a path and with lines the attacker chose (a `.pth` or `profile.d` file runs code on the ship host)

An outsider opens a fork PR whose head branch is named `ship-failed/{FID}`; the refused flush takes it as the leftover branch's open PR, creates no PR of its own, and logs "close PR #N opened but not merged — merge it by hand", pointing the operator at the attacker's PR

Anyone who can push `ship-failed/{FID}` or `ship-close/{FID}` gets a new skill (`.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` plus scripts), a `skills-lock.json` source, a `docs/*.md` rule or a `.bkit/issues.jsonl` `SHIPPED` row onto `dev`, inside bkit's own `[skip ci]` record commit, because the leftover-tip check allows every min-push path instead of the paths a record holds

A leftover tip carrying content the landing gate would reject (a malformed ledger row, a home-directory path, or a secret a consumer's `bkit:gate:min` scans for) reaches `dev` unchecked: `checkLanding` gated only the record, the merge commit is pushed without a gate, and the `[skip ci]` squash subject means no CI runs after it either

Anyone who can push a branch named `x/refs/heads/ship-failed/{FID}` makes `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/ship-failed/{FID}` answer with that look-alike's tip, because `ls-remote` treats the ref as a tail-matched glob; the flush then reads the wrong tip and fails with "cannot fetch origin's ship-failed/{FID}", or merges the look-alike's commit

challengeFindings.title: A `bkit:gate:min` that rewrites a file of the merged leftover tip and exits 0 lets `closePr` push the unrewritten merge commit, where `checkLanding` stops the same landing with "landing gate changed the checkout"

A squash-merged `ship-failed/{FID}` or `ship-close/{FID}` branch left on origin is merged into the next record, and the merge puts back the `.bkit/friction.jsonl` rows that harvest drained from `dev` after that squash, so the new PR lands the drained rows on `dev` again

`gateMerged` compares the merge with `origin/dev` as it reads after the refused push, so when another landing in the same clone has fetched a newer `dev` meanwhile, the record looks like it reverts that newer `dev` code: the flush runs the full push gate, or stops with "has no declared landing gate" when none is declared

Anyone who can push `ship-failed/{FID}` or `ship-close/{FID}` adds `docs/plans/x/y/logs/{FID}/.prettierrc.mjs` and a `.md` file beside it; the record-path check admits both, and `gateMerged` then runs `bkit:gate:min` (here `prettier --check .`) on the merged checkout, so Prettier imports the planted file and runs the attacker's code on the ship host with the operator's environment

Anyone who can push `ship-failed/{FID}` or `ship-close/{FID}` deletes ledger history on `dev`: a leftover tip that removes rows from `docs/decisions.jsonl`, deletes `docs/knowledge.jsonl` or empties another feature's `status.jsonl` (resetting its `dev-dispatch` budget) passes the record-path check and merges cleanly, because the check limits which paths change, not how they change
